message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of move‑in condition; take photos or videos. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must keep premises in good repair and free from health hazards. | • Report problems promptly; keep written records. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withholding** | • If landlord fails to fix major repairs, tenant may pay the repair cost and deduct it from rent, or withhold rent until repaired. | • Document repairs, keep receipts. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot disturb tenant’s peaceful use of the property. | • Unreasonable entry or harassment is prohibited. | | **Entry Notice** | • Landlord must give at least 24 hours written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep copies of notices. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if longer than one year.
• Must include rent amount, due date, security deposit, and lease duration. | • Verify all terms are spelled out. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File complaints with the Texas Commission on Human Rights if discrimination occurs. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the proper eviction procedure: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment), file a complaint in court, and obtain a judgment. | • Tenants can contest eviction in court; they have the right to a hearing. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on rent increases, but must comply with lease terms and give proper notice. | • Check lease for notice period requirements. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide hot water, electricity, and other utilities unless otherwise specified. | • Verify utility responsibilities in lease. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Tenant may sublet or assign only with landlord’s consent, unless lease prohibits it. | • Obtain written permission. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord responsible for common areas (hallways, stairwells, elevators). | • Report maintenance issues. | | **Right to Dispute Charges** | • Tenant can dispute charges for damages or late fees if not justified. | • Keep receipts and documentation. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Take photos/videos of the unit when you move in and when you move out. Keep written records of all communications with your landlord. 2. **Know Your Lease** – Read the lease carefully. If something is unclear, ask for clarification before signing. 3. **Report Problems Promptly** – Send written notices (email or certified mail) for repairs or complaints. Keep copies. 4. **Keep Receipts** – For any repairs you pay yourself, keep receipts and invoices. 5. **Seek Legal Advice** – If you face eviction or believe your landlord is violating your rights, consult a lawyer or a local tenant advocacy group. 6. **File Complaints** – If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). 7. **Know the Eviction Timeline** – Understand the notice periods required for different reasons (nonpayment, lease violation, etc.). --- #### Quick Reference Checklist - [ ] Lease is in writing (if >1 year). - [ ] Security deposit ≤ 2 months’ rent (unfurnished) or 1 month (furnished). - [ ] Landlord provides hot water, electricity, and maintains structure. - [ ] Landlord gives 24‑hour notice before entry. - [ ] Landlord follows proper eviction procedure. - [ ] No discrimination in housing. If you need more detailed guidance or help drafting a lease or a notice, let me know!
